title: Surprise!
coreMove: Build plans that expect the future to contain events your evidence cannot name yet.
sourcePressure: History is often steered by shocks, and recent calm makes people underestimate what has not happened lately.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using history as a script for precise prediction.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening Surprise! with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the surprise move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of surprise and history

exampleSpecs.domain: a port authority planning for cargo shocks after years of steady volume
exampleSpecs.audience: a logistics planner resisting the comfort of recent stability
exampleSpecs.stakes: one unseen disruption can freeze a city's supply chain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she removes the last five calm years from the forecast and asks what would still work if the next shock is unlike the last one
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a harbor forecast map dotted with ships waiting offshore

exampleSpecs.domain: a university endowment committee revising assumptions after a decade of rising markets
exampleSpecs.stakes: tuition support becomes fragile if calm markets are treated as law
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he adds a surprise column to the model before approving the spending rate
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a projection model open on a trustee room screen

exampleSpecs.domain: a wildfire insurance analyst refusing to model only recent burn maps
exampleSpecs.audience: an analyst whose data underweights new climate patterns
exampleSpecs.stakes: premiums and coverage may fail households in the next unlike event
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she overlays old fire maps with new wind corridors before signing the pricing memo
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a transparent wind map laid over a county burn map

exampleSpecs.domain: a board game publisher ordering inventory after three predictable holiday seasons
exampleSpecs.audience: a production manager planning for surprises in demand and shipping
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rigid order can strand cash or miss sales
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks the team to name the surprise that is absent from the spreadsheet before choosing print quantity
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a prototype box beside a freight quote and holiday calendar

exampleSpecs.domain: a public health clinic stocking supplies after a quiet flu season
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic director avoiding recency bias
exampleSpecs.stakes: low recent use may tempt cuts just before a different outbreak
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she reviews which supply ran out during the last unlike surge before reducing anything
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a supply shelf tag with last year's low usage count

exampleSpecs.domain: an estate lawyer helping a client plan beyond the family arrangement that currently feels permanent
exampleSpecs.audience: a lawyer making room for future conflict without predicting it
exampleSpecs.stakes: a will based on today's harmony can fail after remarriage, illness, or distance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks which relationship change would make the current document unfair before drafting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blank beneficiary form under a desk lamp
